King County Washington Inmate Lookup — Official Guide

If you need to locate an inmate in King County Washington, the official King County Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention provides public access to inmate records through their online system. Finding information about someone in custody has never been more straightforward with the county's dedicated lookup tools and resources.

How to Search King County Jail Records

  1. Visit the King County Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention official website
  2. Navigate to the "Inmate Lookup" or "Inmate Search" section on the homepage
  3. Enter the inmate's first and last name in the search field
  4. Select the facility if you know which King County jail location holds the person (Seattle-area facilities include the King County Jail downtown and various holding areas)
  5. Click "Search" to retrieve available records
  6. Review the inmate information displayed, which typically includes booking date, charges, bail amount, and custody status
  7. Note the inmate number for future reference if needed
  8. Contact the facility directly if you need additional details not available online

Bail Information for King County Washington

When someone is arrested in King County Washington, bail amounts are typically set during an initial appearance before a judge, usually within 72 hours of booking. The bail amount depends on factors including the severity of charges, criminal history, ties to the community, and flight risk. Defendants can be released on their own recognizance, posted bail through a bail bondsman (who typically charges 10-15% of the bail amount), or held without bail if deemed a danger or flight risk. King County uses a standard bail schedule, but judges may adjust amounts based on individual circumstances. Family members can post bail directly at the King County Jail, or work with a licensed bail bond agent serving the Seattle-area and surrounding King County jurisdictions.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take for someone to appear in the King County inmate system after arrest?

Typically, a person appears in the King County inmate lookup system within 1-3 hours after booking, though this can vary depending on processing times at the facility.

Can I visit an inmate at King County Jail?

Yes, King County allows visitation at designated times. You'll need to check the specific facility's visitation schedule and rules. Visitors must pass security screening, and some facilities have restrictions on children or require advance notice.

What if I can't find someone in the King County inmate lookup?

If someone isn't appearing in the system, they may have been released, transferred to another facility, or not yet booked. Contact the King County Sheriff's Office directly at the main line or check the King County Superior Court records for case status.
